issues.legal_issue: The government’s revisional jurisdiction extends to a final order of a municipal authority even when municipal law provides no appeal from that order.
material_facts: A municipal authority ordered that proceedings concerning construction contrary to approved plans be compounded upon payment of a fine.
The municipal law provided no appeal from the compounding order.
An aggrieved neighbour asked the government to set the order aside, and the government did so under the statutory revision provision.
The High Court held that the government lacked revisional jurisdiction because the municipal order was not appealable.
issues.conclusion: The government had jurisdiction to entertain a revision against the municipal authority’s non-appealable order. The High Court’s contrary ruling was set aside, and the case was remanded for consideration of the other objections to the government’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(iii) and 2(iv) of the Rajasthan City Municipal Appeals (Regulation) Act, 1950, a municipal appeal is an appeal provided by municipal law to an authority outside the municipality, and the relevant municipal officeholder was a municipal authority. Section 3 transfers such appeals to the Commissioner. Section 4(1) bars further appeals from the Commissioner’s appellate orders but its proviso empowers the government to call for the record of a case and review an order passed by either a Commissioner or a municipal authority. The proviso is an independent legislative provision providing an alternative remedy and covers a wider field than the main part of section 4(1), including final municipal orders for which no appeal lies. Clear operative words cannot be omitted or restricted by reference to the preamble, long title, or a perceived purpose of protecting local autonomy; the preamble may resolve ambiguity but cannot eliminate operative words. The judgment identifies no earlier cases by name as a basis for this ruling.

predicates.case_is_judicial_challenge_to_revision: The proceeding challenges a government decision made after it considered revising a municipal order.
predicates.challenged_order_was_made_by_municipal_a: A municipal authority made the order whose treatment is challenged.
predicates.challenged_order_was_not_appealable_unde: The applicable municipal law provided no appeal from the challenged order.
predicates.review_clause_covers_municipal_authority: The governing review provision authorizes the government to examine orders passed by municipal authorities.

issues.definition: When a judicial challenge concerns government revision of a non-appealable order made by a municipal authority and the governing review clause covers such orders, the government has revision jurisdiction over that order.
